page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, this instance demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core CPU stress tests, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, both for small cached blocks and large uncached blocks, fall within the average tier. Cryptographic and compression workloads, such as AES encryption, SHA-NI, and single-threaded gzip compression, also perform at average levels. For language model workloads, the server achieves strong text generation speeds in the top 25% for small 135M models, though prompt processing and medium 7B model inference remain average.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents a compute-focused hardware profile designed for resource-dense processing tasks. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without virtualization steal, making it suitable for multi-threaded compilation, web serving, and database operations. The inclusion of a local 500 GB NVMe SSD supports workloads requiring fast local read and write access, such as intermediate ETL processing, caching layers, and active database hosting.
description: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, utilizing an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. This compute-optimized instance features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 16 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled 500 GB local NVMe SSD. In benchmark testing, the server delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10%, while multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform at average levels. It also shows strong text generation speeds for small language models. Lacking a GPU, this server is designed for CPU-bound workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation and local NVMe storage make it highly suitable for software compilation, static web serving, database hosting, and medium-scale data processing tasks.
